title: Microsoft Entra: account recovery through government ID verification (Web)
summary: The recovery policy, licensing requirements and roadmap facts are supported by Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections should clarify that the profile path opens its creation wizard, cite the evaluation-mode API property reference, and reconcile the checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: Account recovery restores organisational account access when all registered authentication methods have been lost.
claims.quote: enables users to regain access to their organizational accounts when they've lost access to all registered authentication methods.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes identity verification and trust re-establishment before replacing authentication methods rather than simple credential recovery.
claims.quote: account recovery focuses on identity verification and trust re-establishment prior to replacement of authentication methods rather than simple credential recovery.

claims.claim: Microsoft also lists ID Account Recovery as roadmap item 529857.
claims.quote: Record 529857: "title": "Microsoft Entra: ID Account Recovery"; "description": "Self-Serv Account Recovery for tenants using Passkey.Account Recovery from Total Loss using Verified ID with Face Check".

claims.claim: Roadmap item 529857 covers Android, Desktop and iOS.
claims.quote: Record 529857: "platforms": ["Android", "Desktop", "iOS"].

claims.claim: Roadmap item 529857 targets June CY2026.
claims.quote: Record 529857: "targetDate": "June CY2026".

claims.claim: Recovery is admin-opt-in because the tenant policy is disabled by default for new and existing tenants.
claims.quote: In the new Account recovery policy experience, the policy is disabled by default for both new and existing tenants. Enable the policy before users can use account recovery.

claims.claim: Licensing is mixed: an Entra entitlement, Face Check entitlement and separately purchased provider services.
claims.quote: Users need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license to use account recovery. A Face Check license is also required, either through Entra Suite or standalone. The identity verification provider cost depends on the offer you subscribe to in the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.quote: Users need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license to use account recovery.

claims.quote: A Face Check license is also required, either through Entra Suite or standalone.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The identity verification provider is purchased separately through the Microsoft Security Store.
claims.quote: If your scenario uses an identity verification provider, purchase the provider's services separately through the Microsoft Security Store. These services aren't included in the Microsoft Entra licenses listed in the table.

claims.claim: The licensing page describes Face Check as an add-on included in Microsoft Entra Suite.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra Verified ID also provides Face Check as a premium feature available as an add-on. Face Check is included as a full capability in the Microsoft Entra Suite.

claims.claim: The identity verification provider's cost depends on the subscribed offer.
claims.quote: The identity verification provider cost depends on the offer you subscribe to in the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.claim: Variable cost reflects provider verification costs rather than a claim of no direct charge.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A user starts recovery by selecting Recover your account at sign-in.
claims.quote: If you're unable to sign in with any methods, select Recover your account.

claims.claim: Recovery redirects the user to the organisation's configured identity verification provider.
claims.quote: The user is redirected to the identity verification provider specified in their applicable profile.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The provider verifies government-issued identification.
claims.quote: The provider verifies government-issued identification documents using advanced fraud detection.

claims.claim: Face Check verifies proof of presence against the government ID photo.
claims.quote: Account recovery first verifies proof of presence by comparing the photo on the user's government-issued ID to a real-time Face Check.

claims.claim: The user presents the resulting Verified ID to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: The user presents their newly acquired Verified ID to Microsoft Entra ID. The system validates the credential's authenticity.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; controls[0].note
claims.claim: TAP issuance is on by default when recovery is enabled.
claims.quote: TAP issuance is on by default for new and existing tenants. This default controls the registration path when recovery is enabled; it doesn't enable the tenant's Account recovery policy.

claims.claim: The default recovery journey leads to registering replacement authentication methods such as passkeys.
claims.quote: By default, the user receives a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) with limited validity and is guided through registering new authentication methods, such as passkeys.

claims.claim: Learn labels the settings blade Settings (preview).
claims.quote: Open Settings (preview).

claims.claim: Disabling TAP issuance to register without a TAP is an explicit preview option.
claims.quote: Issue Temporary Access Pass off | Explicit preview opt-in. Successful account validation grants access to registration in the same recovery session without a TAP on supported devices.

claims.claim: Profile management is separate from tenant enablement and actions after recovery.
claims.quote: Profile configuration isn't part of the Account recovery settings blade. Creating a profile doesn't enable the tenant's Account recovery policy or choose actions after recovery.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing identity verification profiles alone do not enable the new tenant policy.
claims.quote: Existing identity verification profiles alone don't enable the new policy.

claims.claim: Tenants using an earlier preview must enable the new policy to continue recovery.
claims.quote: If your tenant already uses account recovery from an earlier preview, you also need to enable the new policy to continue using the feature.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Evaluation mode tests verification without recovering accounts.
claims.quote: Evaluation — Users can test the identity verification flow to confirm it works correctly. Accounts are not recovered in this mode.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Production mode permits verified users in scope to complete recovery.
claims.quote: Production — Users who complete identity verification can fully recover their accounts, receive a Temporary Access Pass by default, and re-enroll authentication methods.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: An optional custom authentication extension validates verified claims against organisation-owned records.
claims.quote: Use a custom authentication extension to validate verified claims against your organization's records. The extension can supplement directory matching or replace it entirely.

claims.claim: Learn describes automated identity proofing as reducing dependence on manual help desk verification.
claims.quote: Account recovery uses automated identity proofing to reduce reliance on manual help desk verification.

claims.claim: Learn warns that social engineering can manipulate support staff into granting access.
claims.quote: Social engineering attacks can manipulate support staff into granting unauthorized access.

claims.claim: Third-party identity verification processes government documents and biometric data.
claims.quote: Identity verification involves processing government-issued documents and biometric data through third-party providers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Providers have their own privacy and data retention policies.
claims.quote: Identity verification providers have their own privacy and data retention policies as part of the verification offer from the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.claim: Data processed by the custom extension stays within the organisation's trust boundary.
claims.quote: Data processed by the custom authentication extension stays within the organization's trust boundary.

claims.claim: Only the extension's match result returns to the recovery flow.
claims.quote: only the match result is returned to the account recovery flow.

claims.claim: The extension does not share organisational data with Microsoft.
claims.quote: No organizational data is shared with Microsoft

claims.claim: Learn warns that name-only matching may be insufficient for high-risk accounts.
claims.quote: For sensitive user populations, consider enabling a custom authentication extension to validate additional claims beyond first and last name. Name-only matching may not provide sufficient assurance for high-risk accounts.

claims.claim: Excluded groups apply across all identity verification profiles.
claims.quote: Exclude applies globally across all identity verification profiles, not just the profile you're editing.

claims.claim: Creating a profile turns on Verified ID as an authentication method for all users.
claims.quote: Creating a profile also turns on Verified ID as an authentication method for all users.

claims.claim: Stale credential cleanup becomes available when TAP issuance is turned off.
claims.quote: Issue Temporary Access Pass off | Explicit preview opt-in. ... Stale-credential cleanup becomes available.

claims.claim: Explicitly enabled cleanup deletes previous authentication methods after successful recovery and replacement-passkey registration.
claims.quote: Off by default; explicitly opt in during preview with TAP issuance off. After successful recovery and replacement-passkey registration, deletes all previously registered authentication methods while preserving the new passkey.

claims.claim: Cleanup preserves the replacement passkey.
claims.quote: deletes all previously registered authentication methods while preserving the new passkey.

claims.claim: Cleanup failure does not make recovery fail.
claims.quote: If deletion fails, recovery remains successful.

claims.claim: Users can recover independently without a help desk step after successful verification and validation in Production mode.
claims.quote: Users recover accounts independently without waiting for help desk availability, reducing downtime during critical situations.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Conditional Access requirements unsupported for onboarding and recovery can block the recovery journey.
claims.quote: Conditional Access policies can block account recovery if they require controls that aren't supported for the onboarding and recovery user action.

claims.claim: Require authentication strength is unsupported for the onboarding and recovery user action.
claims.quote: The following controls aren't supported for these journeys: ... Require authentication strength.

claims.claim: Terms of use is unsupported for the onboarding and recovery user action.
claims.quote: The following controls aren't supported for these journeys: Terms of use.

claims.claim: First-name or last-name mismatches can prevent account validation and TAP issuance.
claims.quote: This error may be present when account ownership couldn't be confirmed—often due to mismatches between the first and last names in the user's profile and those on the ID.

claims.claim: B2B users are not supported.
claims.quote: Account recovery doesn't support B2B users, external guest users, or federated users.

claims.claim: External guest users are not supported.
claims.quote: Account recovery doesn't support B2B users, external guest users, or federated users.

claims.claim: Federated users are not supported.
claims.quote: Account recovery doesn't support B2B users, external guest users, or federated users.

claims.claim: When passkey attestation is required, TAP-free registration is supported only on Android.
claims.quote: When your organization requires passkey attestation, registration without a TAP is supported only on Android. On iOS, you continue to receive a TAP

claims.claim: Recovery is designed for accounts with prior authentication events.
claims.quote: Account recovery is designed for actively used accounts that have prior authentication events.

claims.claim: Users may need an initial authentication after enabling or changing recovery scope before seeing the recovery option.
claims.quote: After you enable or change the scope of account recovery, users might need to complete an initial authentication before the recovery option is made available.

claims.claim: Authentication Policy Administrator manages Account recovery settings.
claims.quote: The Authentication Policy Administrator role to manage Account recovery settings.

claims.claim: Profile creation accepts Authentication Policy Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: The Authentication Policy Administrator or Global Administrator role in the tenant.

claims.claim: Authentication Policy Administrator is the least-privilege role for creating profiles.
claims.quote: Use Authentication Policy Administrator for least privilege. Use Global Administrator only if no other role combination meets your needs.
